key_insight: An OMOP-standardized prostate cancer EHR database can be strengthened by NLP and PSA-based algorithms to recover missing diagnosis, pathology, treatment, and recurrence data.
clinical_relevance: This approach may improve prostate cancer research data quality and make real-world EHR data more usable alongside cancer registry records.
method: Converted UTMB Epic EHR prostate cancer records into OMOP CDM v5.4
Used NLP to extract PSA, Gleason score, and cancer stage from clinical text
Applied PSA-based algorithms to identify missing treatments and biochemical recurrence
evidence_signal: Among 815 analytic cases, 700 (85.9%) were complete and concordant with registry data, with PSA showing excellent agreement and NLP substantially improving sparse structured fields.
watch_item: Performance depends on local EHR structure, note quality, and registry accuracy, so manual review and site-specific validation are still needed.
paper_title: Developing an OMOP-Standardized Prostate Cancer Database and Improving Data Quality Using NLP and PSA-Based Algorithms
